summary: Matthew B. Orsborn specializes in Buddhist studies, completing his PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2012 under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. In 2026, he was Professor and Head of the International Affairs Section at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Matthew Clark works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London between 1999 and 2004, studying under Daud Ali and George Botterill.
Matthew Immergut, a scholar in sociology and Buddhist studies, studied under Culadasa. In 2011, he served as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew MacKenzie works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1996–2004) and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Colorado State University in 2008.

Matthew R. Sayers is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008). He held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Helen Baroni and Michel Mohr, and a PhD from Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe (attested 2015).

Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Brown University (1987) and held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (ca. 1989–1996), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2002).
Matthew Thomson Adam worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary teacher for the London Missionary Society from 1820 to 1830 and as a teacher at Presidency University until 1830.

Matthew W. King works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto in 2014 under the supervision of Frances Garrett, also studying under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thubten Champa.

Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki / Imperial Alexander University from ca. 1830 to 1836 and held a post there from ca. 1840 to 1852.

Matthias Christian Sprengel (1746–1803) studied history and Indology at Rostock, Bützow, and Göttingen. He served as professor of history at the University of Göttingen (1778) and as University Librarian at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1778–1801).

Matthias Hermanns (1899–1972) was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Fribourg (1946–1948). He later taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1950–1954) and the Steyler Missionswissenschaftliches Institut (1960–1968).

Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a Dutch linguist who studied at Leiden University (ca. 1838–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his PhD from Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1860. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1863, 1866), University of Würzburg (1868), and University of Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a doctorate in molecular biology from the Pasteur Institute (ca. 1972) and has served as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

Mattia Salvini works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski (ca. 2004–2010). He has held positions at Mahidol University (attested 2011) and the International Buddhist College.

Mauli Chand Prasad works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Maureen L. P. Patterson (1930–2019) was an Indologist who studied under W. Norman Brown. She served as South Asia Librarian at the University of Chicago (attested in 1984 and 2007).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at Johns Hopkins University under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He spent his career as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) was a French linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Paris (ca. 1890–1895). He served at the University of Burgundy (1892–1895) and as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at the University of Montpellier (1895–1939).
